name: BackupMaster
summary: Automatic daily backups for Shopify: products, collections, themes, blogs, pages, files, metafields, metaobjects, translations, customers, orders and inventory, with 365-day retention and one-click restore; Pro adds downloadable copies, Google Drive sync and store duplication for staging.
best_for: Shopify stores under roughly 1,500 orders a month that want the whole store backed up daily (metafields, metaobjects and translations included) without anyone having to remember to trigger it
skip_if: you need backups exported to storage you control on the entry tier, retention you can configure beyond one year, or orders you can restore, which BackupMaster's own documentation says are backup-only
honest_knock:
The listing header says free to install, and there is a free tier, but it is not for you unless you are an agency: Agency is limited to Shopify Partner development stores before they are handed over to a client. For a live store the entry price is $19 a month and it buys 300 orders a month.

Restore is described on the listing as restoring supported items, and the list of what that excludes lives in the documentation rather than on the listing. It matters. Read on 10 October 2026, the coverage page says orders are backed up but cannot be restored or cloned, because Shopify limits updates to existing orders. Locations, saved searches, policies and shipping zones are backup-only, and inventory comes back only through a manual download and Shopify's own inventory import. Store settings, third-party app data, reviews, redirects, coupons, companies, catalogs and analytics are not covered at all. Read that page before you rely on the product, and run one real restore into a development store rather than discovering the boundary during an incident.

The most useful review on the page is the critical one. In April 2026 a merchant asked for exports over SFTP to storage the vendor does not control, on-demand backups before risky changes, configurable retention and languages beyond English and German. The same merchant noted that a second store costs extra here where some rivals include one. None of that is damning; it is a fair map of where this app currently stops. One of those requests has since been met in part: the documentation now describes a Backup Now button for a manual backup at any time (read 10 October 2026). Worth adding to the same note: your store data sits with a vendor in Australia, which belongs in your processing register whatever you decide.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Essentials · per month for a live store up to 300 orders a month
pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/backup-master) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial. Agency is free to install but only for Shopify Partner development stores before they are transferred to a client, with all features enabled for three months. Essentials $19 a month or $205.20 a year, a 10% saving, covers stores up to 300 orders a month. That is automatic daily backups of products, collections, themes, blogs, pages, files, metafields, metaobjects, translations, customers, orders and inventories, restore of supported items, 365-day retention and unlimited cloud storage. Pro $39 a month or $421.20 a year covers up to 600 orders a month and adds downloadable backup copies, Google Drive sync and duplication of data for staging or expansion. Plus $79 a month or $853.20 a year covers up to 1,500 orders a month, and adds multi-store pricing, detailed audit logs, external portal access, a custom backup time and priority support. The listing says higher-volume plans exist on the vendor's own pricing page without printing what they cost. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer BackupMaster, Bondi, NSW, Australia; the app launched 4 August 2017, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge, is available in English and German, and had 108 reviews at the time of writing. Read again on 10 October 2026: the four tiers and their prices are unchanged and the listing showed 124 reviews at 4.8. backupmaster.io/pricing lists further order bands from 2,500 to more than 1,000,000 orders a month without printing their prices, says it does not auto-upgrade, and offers refunds within 7 days of the first purchase depending on usage, with renewals not refundable. Read again on 19 November 2026 on the listing and on www.backupmaster.io/pricing (the bare backupmaster.io address timed out that day): the four tiers, their prices, the order caps and the 7-day refund terms are unchanged, and the listing showed 123 reviews at 4.8.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested BackupMaster on a Shopify development store: the install, the plan page, and the free Agency Plan (all features for 3 months), which started the first backup by itself. The products (23 items) were backed up in about 1 minute, Collections, Metafield definitions and Metaobjects finished after that, and Themes and Assets were still running. The version screen of one product was looked at, and no restore was run. Essentials, Pro and Plus were greyed out because this store is unpublished, so there was no Shopify payment screen and nothing was paid. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the app was installed through the App Store form in our own tab at 17:08; the dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. The app is called BackupMaster Backups in the admin, the admin was in English, and the welcome screen said that the app backs up the store data and allows you to restore it, and to choose a subscription plan to get started. Plans: the plan page says the pricing plans are based on the average number of orders, and that this store averaged 0 orders per month over the past three months. The Agency Plan is exclusively for agencies and developers with partner development stores, with full feature access for 3 months, a partner program (inquire for details), and the note that after the store is transferred the owner must choose a plan to keep using the app. Essentials is $19.00 USD a month for up to 300 orders a month, Pro is $39.00 USD a month for up to 600 orders a month and Plus is $79.00 USD a month for up to 1500 orders a month (a list lets you pick the order band); there is a Monthly and an Annual switch that was not looked at. All three paid plans had a greyed out Choose this plan button with a tooltip: This plan isn't available for unpublished stores. So none of them could be chosen on this store, and the paid plans, their trial and their billing were not seen. Core action, a backup of the products: we chose the Agency Plan (Choose this plan). There was no Shopify payment screen, no card and no charge to approve; the app went straight to its dashboard, and the first backup started by itself. It showed Backing up your store, Backing up Products and 5 of 23 items backed up. After about 1 minute (about 17:09, 4 clicks after the install) it said Products: 23 items backed up with the label Finished. Then Collections said 3 items backed up (Finished), Metafield definitions 22 items backed up (Finished) and Metaobjects 2 items backed up (Finished); Themes and Assets were still running (30 of 946) when we stopped looking, so a full backup was not seen to the end. One screenshot (02) was taken while Metafield definitions were still in progress, before the notes say they finished. Looking at the backup: the product list shows Last edited for each product and a View versions button. For the product Demo Shirt the screen showed the Current item on the left and the Backed-up version 2026-11-17 5:09 PM on the right and a button Restore to this version, greyed out because nothing differed; a banner on top said Bulk operation in progress. The dashboard also has Bulk restore. NO restore was run: it can overwrite the test data of the store. Differences with the dossier: none found. The prices and the order bands of Essentials ($19, 300 orders), Pro ($39, 600 orders) and Plus ($79, 1500 orders) are those of the dossier, and Agency is free for partner development stores with all features for three months, as the dossier says. The dossier also gives a 7-day free trial for each paid tier and yearly prices; neither was seen, because the paid plans could not be chosen. The dossier says the backups are daily; only the first backup was seen. Checkout: NOT reached. The Agency Plan has no payment step and the paid plans are not available for an unpublished store, so no Shopify approval screen, price total, tax or renewal term was observed. Cancelling: no paid subscription was started, so nothing could be cancelled. The way to stop is uninstalling the app: Settings, Apps, the three dots menu, Uninstall opens a dialog with the text that you can no longer use the app and that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required (we chose Testing multiple apps). Not tested: a restore, Clone store, Export, Import, Google Drive sync, any paid plan and the finish of the Themes and Assets backup. No theme change was made and nothing was changed in the store. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at 17:11 through Settings, Apps and it disappeared from Installed; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The paid plans are greyed out on an unpublished store, so only the Agency Plan could be tried and no checkout was seen; the screen of a backed-up version says Bulk operation in progress and limits some functions while the backup runs; a full backup including Themes and Assets was not seen to the end; and the restore was not tried because it can overwrite the store.
